text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The foreign trade deficit during the first half of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) narrowed to $1.66 billion, showing over 20 percent decrease over the year-ago period.
- Prices increased in December with the consumer price index showing a rise of 11.41 percent over December 1995.
- Prices of edible oil are receding to normal in the local market as the supply of crude oil to millers has been resumed by oil tankers from Karachi.
- The Supreme Court has decided to club together the three petitions challenging the dissolution of the National Assembly (lower house) by President Farooq Leghari on November 5.
- One government official has said Pakistan will start exporting cooking oil to the Far East in the coming six months.
- The Cotton Committee expects a crop of nine million 375-lb bales in 1996/97.
- A ship carrying 2,500 tonnes of sugar will berth at Karachi Port Sunday.
- The government is using the proceeds of privatisation of state-controlled assets to finance the budget deficit despite assurances that they will be utilised only to retire public debt.
- Pakistan had a literacy rate of 39 percent in 1995/96, up from 35 percent in 1991.
- The International Monetary Fund has refused to release the second tranche of $80 million standby loan to Pakistan, which was scheduled to be released on January 10.
- Pakistani ginneries have received 7.614 million 375-lb bales of cotton between July 1 and January 9, the Cotton Export Corporation of Pakistan said.
